main_body: Loom frame seen straight on: a brown wooden border with a white warp-thread panel and a red/yellow checker band inside, standing on two legs
top_band: none as a real top surface. Rows 10-12 (brown #b77246 with a #d59147 highlight) are the front face of the top beam. The bottom beam at rows 22-23 uses the same colours, so the two beams mirror each other.
evidence: The column scan at x=8, 16 and 23 shows a 3-row brown top beam, then the thread panel and checker band, then a 2-3 row brown bottom beam in identical tones. No horizontal surface is visible from above, because the top beam is not lighter than the bottom one and has no front-edge step. The dark rim, the side posts and the panel are all painted flat on one plane. The legs are plain vertical strips with no visible top or base surface. This is an architectural front elevation, not a 3/4 drawing.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tinted line (0% neutral edge pixels), which matches Beodeul practice. The piece has only 12 distinct colours, against 40 and 38 in the references. It carries 11 colours per tile, against 17 and 20. The wood ramp has only about 3-4 steps (dark rim, mid, light, highlight). The thread panel is a regular repeating stripe pattern with little grain or per-element shading. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the references, so it fails.
